questions.question: A motorcyclist should always look ahead at the road for:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Look ahead to see changes in traffic, hazards on the road, and possible escape routes. Be ready to react quickly to any changes.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes since it is light outside.
Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you better.
Wear shorts if it is hot for comfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors when riding so other drivers can see you more easily.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cause control problems.
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes creates control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again. If your rear brake locks on good pavement when stopping, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the light will soon turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Having just one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: Will not result in a DUI charge.
Will never affect your riding skills.
Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can harm your riding ability. You can be charged with riding impaired even if your blood alcohol level is below the legal limit.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be seen better when riding, even during the day. Reflective materials on your clothing also help.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather boots
questions.explanation: Leather boots offer the best protection when riding. They should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane ends.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket when it is cold.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket.
questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding, even if the weather is warm.

questions.question: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times to help others see you. Most motorcycles made after 1978 turn on the headlight automatically when running. Check that your headlight works before every ride.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce your chances of an accident by:

options.text: Not using turn signals because they distract other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to others, use turn signals, keep safe distance from other vehicles, watch ahead for hazards, and be ready to react. Always stay alert on the road.

questions.question: After riding over an object on the road, you should:

options.text: Keep riding. The danger is over.
Pull to the side and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop and remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: After hitting an object on the road, pull off to the side and check your tires and rims for damage. Also check that nothing is caught in the drive chain or belt before you continue riding.

questions.question: When riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time, you should:

options.text: Just start riding. Learning by doing is the best way.
Just start riding. Most bikes are the same.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn how the bike works.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn how the bike works.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding a new bike, check its safety and maintenance, locate all controls, and practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes to understand how it handles.

questions.question: When cars are merging from an entrance ramp, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Assume the entering drivers see them.
Never assume the entering drivers see them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume the entering drivers see them.
questions.explanation: Give merging cars plenty of space and never assume drivers see you. Change lanes away from them if you can. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to let them merge safely.

questions.question: Which color will make you less visible to other drivers?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or dull colors while riding.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake and rear brake at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front brake and rear brake at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly and safely, apply steady pressure to both the front and rear brakes at the same time. Be careful not to lock the brakes.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it:
questions.correctAnswerText: Has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Motorcycle mirrors:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.
Do not have blind spots because motorcycles are smaller.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go ahead.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots.
questions.explanation: Leather boots protect your feet the most when riding. Choose boots that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
It can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: How can you become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: The only way to become sober is to give your body time to remove the alcohol. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: How is alcohol different from other substances?

options.text: It enters the bloodstream very quickly.
It must be digested before entering the bloodstream.
It can improve your riding ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It enters the bloodstream very quickly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It enters the bloodstream directly through the stomach and small intestine walls. It quickly reaches and affects the brain.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should matter most to you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Protection.
questions.explanation: Protection should be your main concern when choosing a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider do to reduce the chance of a collision?

options.text: Maintain enough space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain enough space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep a good space cushion around your motorcycle at all times. This includes when following another vehicle, being followed, passing, being passed, or lane sharing.

questions.question: What should you look for in a protective motorcycle jacket?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather or synthetic materials.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket that covers your arms completely and fits snugly but allows you to move freely. Leather or strong synthetic materials with body armor offer the best protection.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what is important to do?

options.text: Focus only on what is in front of you.
Focus only on what is behind you.
Pay attention to what is in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pay attention to what is in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: Watch what is ahead of you, but also pay attention to what is behind you. Check your mirrors often to stay aware of traffic around you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red traffic light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to all crossing traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.
